clues: He was a prophet.
He was the first of the prophets.
He was the first human being.
The angels were commanded to prostrate to him.
He and his wife were placed in the Garden.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, is the first human being and the first prophet. The Qur'an recounts the command to the angels to prostrate to him, and Iblis's refusal.

clues: He was a prophet.
A surah bears his name.
He left his people before he was permitted to.
He was swallowed by a great fish.
He called out from within the darkness and was answered.
easy.explain: Yunus (Jonah), ʿalayhi al-salām, called upon Allah from within the fish with the words known as Du'a Yunus. His people later believed, and the punishment was lifted from them.

clues: He was a prophet.
He lost his wealth and his health.
He is remembered above all for one quality.
That quality is patience in affliction.
He called upon his Lord and was restored.
easy.explain: Ayyub (Job), ʿalayhi al-salām, is the standing example of sabr — patience through severe affliction — and was restored after calling upon his Lord.

clues: He was a prophet and also a king.
His father was also a prophet.
He was given understanding of the speech of birds and other creatures.
The jinn were made subject to him.
A hoopoe brought him news of the Queen of Sheba.
easy.explain: Sulayman (Solomon), ʿalayhi al-salām, son of Dawud, was given a kingdom and understanding of the speech of creatures. Surah An-Naml recounts the episode of the hoopoe and Bilqis.

clues: He was a prophet and a king.
He was given a scripture.
That scripture is the Zabur.
Iron was made pliable for him.
As a young man he defeated Jalut.
easy.explain: Dawud (David), ʿalayhi al-salām, was given the Zabur and a kingdom. The Qur'an mentions iron being made pliable for him and his victory over Jalut (Goliath).

clues: It is a place in the hereafter.
Belief in it is part of Islamic belief.
It is the opposite of the Garden.
It is a place of punishment.
It is the Fire.
easy.explain: Jahannam is the Fire, the place of punishment in the hereafter, the opposite of Jannah.

clues: He is a created being.
He is not an angel but of the jinn.
He refused a command out of arrogance.
That command was to prostrate to Adam.
He was granted respite to misguide.
easy.explain: Iblis refused the command to prostrate to Adam out of arrogance. The Qur'an states he was of the jinn, not the angels.

clues: It is a phrase of remembrance.
It is said very frequently.
It is often said after the prayer.
It declares Allah free of all imperfection.
The phrase is SubhanAllah.
easy.explain: Tasbih is saying SubhanAllah, declaring Allah free of any imperfection. Tahmid is Alhamdulillah, takbir is Allahu akbar, and tahlil is La ilaha illa Allah.

clues: It is a short phrase.
It opens every prayer.
It is repeated at each change of position in the prayer.
It is called out during the two Eids.
The phrase is Allahu akbar.
easy.explain: The takbir, Allahu akbar, opens the prayer and marks each change of posture within it. It is also called out during the days of Eid.

clues: They are reports, not a single book.
They were collected and graded by scholars.
Each has a chain of transmission.
They record what the Prophet ﷺ said and did.
Al-Bukhari and Muslim compiled famous collections of them.
easy.explain: Hadith are the transmitted reports of the Prophet's sayings, actions and approvals, each with a chain of narrators. They are the means by which the Sunnah is preserved.

clues: It is a ruling category.
It applies to actions and to food.
It is the opposite of haram.
It describes what is permitted.
It is most often heard in relation to food and drink.
easy.explain: Halal means permitted. Haram is the forbidden, makruh the disliked, and mubah the neutral.

clues: It is a title given to a person.
It relates to the Qur'an.
It is not about leading prayer.
It is not about the beauty of recitation.
It describes someone who has memorised the entire Qur'an.
easy.explain: A hafiz is one who has memorised the whole Qur'an. A qari is a skilled reciter, an imam leads prayer, and a mu'adhdhin calls the adhan.

clues: It is a division of the Qur'an.
It does not follow chapter boundaries.
It exists to help with reading and memorising.
There are thirty of them.
Many people read one each night in Ramadan.
easy.explain: The Qur'an is divided into thirty ajza of roughly equal length, which is why many complete a full reading over the thirty nights of Ramadan.

clues: It is a form of remembrance.
It is said at any time.
It is especially encouraged after wrongdoing.
It is also said after completing acts of worship.
It is seeking forgiveness from Allah.
easy.explain: Istighfar is seeking Allah's forgiveness, commonly with the phrase Astaghfirullah. It is encouraged both after wrongdoing and as regular remembrance.

clues: It is a feature of a mosque.
It is on one particular wall.
It is usually a recess or niche.
It shows the congregation which way to face.
The imam stands in front of it.
easy.explain: The mihrab is the niche in the qiblah wall of a mosque indicating the direction of prayer. The minbar is the pulpit used for the sermon.

clues: It is a feature of a mosque.
It is usually raised, with steps.
It is not used during the obligatory prayer.
It is used once a week in particular.
The khutbah is delivered from it.
easy.explain: The minbar is the raised pulpit from which the Friday sermon is delivered.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was the brother of another prophet.
He was known for his eloquence of speech.
His brother asked Allah to appoint him as a helper.
That brother was Musa.
easy.explain: Harun (Aaron), ʿalayhi al-salām, was the brother of Musa, appointed as his helper at Musa's own request because of his clearer speech.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was a son of Ibrahim.
He was left as an infant in a barren valley.
The well of Zamzam sprang for him.
He helped his father raise the foundations of the Ka'bah.
easy.explain: Isma'il (Ishmael), ʿalayhi al-salām, son of Ibrahim and Hajar, is connected with Zamzam and with the raising of the Ka'bah's foundations alongside his father.

clues: It is an obligatory charity.
It is not the one given at the end of Ramadan.
It is calculated rather than fixed per person.
It becomes due after a lunar year has passed.
It is the zakat on accumulated wealth.
easy.explain: Zakat al-Mal is the zakat on wealth, due annually on holdings above the nisab. Zakat al-Fitr is the smaller fixed amount given per person before the Eid prayer.

clues: It is a position in the prayer.
It is the first position of each rak'ah.
Al-Fatihah is recited in it.
It is the tallest of the positions.
It is simply standing.
easy.explain: Qiyam is the standing position of the prayer, in which Al-Fatihah and a further passage are recited.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of 96 ayahs.
It is surah 56, falling in juz 27.
Its name refers to an event that must come.
It divides people into three groups.
Those groups are the foremost, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah (56) describes the Inevitable Event and divides humanity into three categories: the foremost, the companions of the right hand, and the companions of the left.

clues: It is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
It has three ayahs.
It is a Makkan surah.
It was revealed as consolation to the Prophet ﷺ.
Its name refers to abundance granted to him.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kawthar (108) is the shortest surah at three ayahs. It was revealed as consolation, affirming that it is the Prophet's detractor who is cut off.

clues: It is a form of purification.
It is more complete than the usual ablution.
It is required in specific states.
It involves washing the whole body.
It is recommended before Jumu'ah and the two Eids.
medium.explain: Ghusl is the complete washing of the body, obligatory in certain states and recommended before Jumu'ah, the two Eids and entering ihram.

clues: It is a means of purification.
It is used only in particular circumstances.
It does not involve water at all.
It is permitted when water is unavailable or harmful.
It is performed with clean earth or dust.
medium.explain: Tayammum is dry purification with clean earth, permitted when water is unavailable or its use would cause harm.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of eleven ayahs.
It is surah 62.
It is named after a day.
It commands leaving off trade when the call is made.
It instructs the believers to hasten to the remembrance of Allah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Jumu'ah (62) commands the believers to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah when the Friday call to prayer is made.

clues: It is a boundary, not a building.
It concerns pilgrims approaching Makkah.
There are several of them in different directions.
A pilgrim may not pass it in ordinary clothes if intending the rites.
It is where ihram is entered.
medium.explain: The mawaqit are the fixed points around Makkah at which pilgrims coming from different directions must enter the state of ihram.

clues: It is a calendar.
It has twelve months.
Its months are determined by the moon.
Its year is about eleven days shorter than the solar year.
Its count begins from the migration to Madinah.
medium.explain: The Hijri calendar is lunar, with twelve months and a year of about 354 days, counted from the year of the Hijrah in 622 CE.

clues: It was fought between Muslims.
It took place during the first fitnah.
It was in the caliphate of Ali.
It was fought near Basra in 36 AH.
It takes its name from the animal Aisha rode during it.
medium.explain: The Battle of the Camel, 36 AH, was fought near Basra during the first fitnah. It takes its name from the camel on which Aisha was present at the battle.

clues: The term refers to two surahs together.
They are both very short.
They are the final two in the mushaf.
Both begin with the command: Say, I seek refuge.
They are Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
medium.explain: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn, the two surahs of seeking refuge, are Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114), both opening with 'Qul a'udhu'.

clues: It is a rite of Hajj.
It takes place at Mina.
It is performed on the 10th and the days of Tashriq.
It involves small stones.
It is the stoning of the pillars.
medium.explain: Ramy al-Jamarat is the stoning of the three pillars at Mina, performed on the Day of Sacrifice and during the days of Tashriq.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of forty ayahs.
It is surah 78.
It opens the final juz.
Its opening words give that juz its common name.
It begins by asking what they are asking one another about.
medium.explain: Surah An-Naba (78) opens juz 30, which is commonly called Juz Amma after this surah's opening words, 'Amma yatasa'alun'.

clues: It is an alternative name for a surah.
That surah is very short.
It is recited in every unit of prayer.
The name means the Mother of the Book.
The surah is Al-Fatihah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah is known by several names, including Umm al-Kitab, the Mother of the Book, and al-Sab' al-Mathani, the seven oft-repeated verses.

clues: It is the gravest matter in Islamic belief.
It concerns the oneness of Allah.
It is the opposite of tawhid.
Luqman warned his son against it above all else.
It is associating partners with Allah.
medium.explain: Shirk is associating partners with Allah, the gravest violation of tawhid. Surah Luqman records his counsel to his son warning against it.

clues: It is a quality of the believer.
The Qur'an states that provisions should be taken, and the best of them is this.
Surah Al-Hujurat says the most honoured are those with most of it.
It is often rendered as God-consciousness.
It is awareness of Allah leading to mindful conduct.
medium.explain: Taqwa is God-consciousness. Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 states that the most honoured in the sight of Allah is the one with the most taqwa, not the one of highest lineage.

clues: It is a quality of an action, not of a person's knowledge.
It concerns why something is done.
Without it, outward worship is not accepted.
A surah is named with the same word.
It means sincerity, doing an act for Allah alone.
medium.explain: Ikhlas is sincerity of intention — performing an act for Allah alone. The well-known hadith that actions are judged by intentions bears directly on it.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-nine ayahs.
It is surah 57.
It is named after a material.
It mentions that material being sent down with great strength.
That material is iron.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Hadid (57) is named for iron, which it describes as sent down, containing great strength and benefits for people.

clues: It is a term of disapproval in religious matters.
It concerns worship in particular.
It is contrasted with the established practice.
Scholars discuss its categories in detail.
It refers to newly introduced matters in the religion.
medium.explain: Bid'ah refers to newly introduced practices in religious matters without basis in the sources. Scholars differ considerably over how the term should be applied.

clues: It is one of the six articles of faith.
It is often expressed as a pair of words.
It concerns what Allah has decreed.
It does not remove human responsibility.
It is divine decree and destiny.
medium.explain: Belief in divine decree is the sixth article of faith. Islamic theology holds that it does not negate human responsibility or the reality of choice.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-two ayahs.
It is surah 58.
Its name refers to a woman.
It was revealed concerning a woman who argued her case.
She brought her complaint about her husband to the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mujadilah (58) is named for the woman who disputed her case with the Prophet ﷺ concerning her husband, and whose complaint Allah answered.

clues: It is a quality praised throughout the Qur'an.
It is counselled in Surah Al-Asr.
Prophet Ayyub is its clearest example.
It applies in hardship and in obedience alike.
It is patience and steadfastness.
medium.explain: Sabr is patience and steadfastness — in hardship, in obedience, and in restraint from wrongdoing. Surah Al-Asr names mutual counsel to it as one of four saving qualities.

clues: It was a period of internal conflict.
It followed the killing of a caliph.
It fell within the caliphate of Ali.
It included the Battle of the Camel.
It also included Siffin.
hard.explain: The first fitnah was the civil conflict following the killing of Uthman, encompassing the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH and Siffin in 37 AH during Ali's caliphate.

clues: They took place immediately after the Prophet's passing.
They fell within the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
They concerned tribes withdrawing from the new state.
They included the Battle of Yamamah.
They ended with the peninsula reunified.
hard.explain: The Ridda campaigns under Abu Bakr addressed tribes that withheld allegiance or zakat after the Prophet's passing. The Battle of Yamamah was their costliest engagement.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-three ayahs.
It is surah 33.
Its name refers to a confederacy.
It relates to the siege of Madinah.
It also contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ as the seal of the prophets.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ahzab (33) is named for the Confederates who besieged Madinah at Khandaq. It contains 33:40, naming the Prophet ﷺ as the Seal of the Prophets.

clues: He was among the earliest Muslims.
He is one of the ten given glad tidings.
He emigrated twice, to Abyssinia and then Madinah.
He was known for great wealth and generosity.
Umar appointed him to the council that chose the next caliph.
hard.explain: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was among the earliest Muslims and the ten promised Paradise, known for his wealth and generosity, and a member of the shura Umar appointed to select his successor.

clues: It was a council convened to make a decision.
It was set up as a caliph lay dying.
It consisted of six senior companions.
Its task was to select a successor.
Its outcome was the caliphate of Uthman.
hard.explain: Umar appointed a council of six senior companions to choose his successor from among themselves. Their deliberation resulted in the selection of Uthman.

clues: It was a gathering in Madinah.
It took place immediately after the Prophet's passing.
It was initially a meeting of the Ansar.
Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubaydah arrived during it.
It concluded with allegiance given to Abu Bakr.
hard.explain: The gathering at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah immediately after the Prophet's passing concluded with the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr as the first caliph.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-five ayahs.
It is surah 8.
Its name refers to the spoils of war.
It was revealed largely in connection with one battle.
That battle is Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal (8) relates largely to the Battle of Badr and its aftermath, including the distribution of spoils. It is followed by At-Tawbah, the only surah without the Basmalah.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.
It refers to the final portion of the mushaf.
Its surahs are comparatively short.
Scholars differ over exactly where it begins.
It runs to the end of the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Al-Mufassal is the final section of the mushaf, comprising the shorter surahs. Scholars differ on its starting point, commonly given as Surah Qaf or Al-Hujurat.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.
It refers to the opening portion of the mushaf.
It contains seven surahs.
It begins with Al-Baqarah.
Its seventh member is disputed.
hard.explain: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal are the seven long surahs beginning at Al-Baqarah. The seventh is counted either as Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah together, or as Yunus.

clues: He was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ.
He raised him after the death of his grandfather.
He protected him for many years in Makkah.
He did not accept Islam, by the well-known accounts.
He died in the Year of Sorrow.
hard.explain: Abu Talib raised and protected the Prophet ﷺ through the difficult Makkan years. His death, alongside Khadijah's, gave the Year of Sorrow its name.

clues: He was a leading figure of the Quraysh.
He led opposition to the Muslims for years.
He commanded at Uhud.
He did not die in that opposition.
He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
hard.explain: Abu Sufyan led Quraysh opposition for years, including at Uhud, and accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of thirteen ayahs.
It is surah 60.
Its name refers to a woman being examined.
It addresses relations with those outside the community.
It concerns the testing of women who migrated to Madinah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60) addresses loyalty and relations with those outside the community, and the examination of women who emigrated to Madinah.

clues: It is a pair of terms in Qur'anic study.
It concerns the relationship between two texts.
One of them supersedes the other.
Scholars differ widely over how many cases exist.
It is the abrogating and the abrogated.
hard.explain: Nasikh is the abrogating text and mansukh the abrogated. Scholars broadly accept the principle but differ substantially over how many verses it affects.

clues: It is a pair of terms in Qur'anic study.
Surah Al-Imran mentions both in a single verse.
One kind is clear in meaning.
The other admits of more than one reading.
That verse warns against pursuing the second to cause discord.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Imran 3:7 distinguishes the muhkam, verses clear in meaning, from the mutashabih, those that are not, and warns against pursuing the latter to sow discord.

clues: He was a scholar of the later medieval period.
He was born in Tunis and died in 1406.
He served in several courts in North Africa and Egypt.
He is best known for one introductory work.
That work is the Muqaddimah.
hard.explain: Ibn Khaldun (d. 1406) is best known for the Muqaddimah, the introduction to his universal history, widely regarded as a foundational work in historiography and social thought.

clues: She was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
She had earlier migrated to Abyssinia.
She was present at Hudaybiyyah.
Her counsel there resolved a difficult moment.
She advised the Prophet ﷺ to act first and let the people follow.
hard.explain: At Hudaybiyyah, when the companions hesitated to leave ihram, Umm Salamah advised the Prophet ﷺ to perform the act himself first, after which the people followed.

options: The clause on the delayed Umrah
clues: It was a term of a written agreement.
That agreement was concluded in 6 AH.
It concerned the cessation of hostilities.
It was the term with the longest horizon.
It set a period of ten years.
hard.explain: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah established a ten-year truce. Its other terms included the postponement of the Umrah by a year and provisions on those who crossed between the two sides.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of thirty-eight ayahs.
It is surah 47.
It is named after a person.
It is sometimes also called Surah al-Qital.
It is the only surah bearing the Prophet's name.
hard.explain: Surah Muhammad (47) is the only surah named after the Prophet ﷺ. It is also known as Surah al-Qital for its subject matter.

clues: He was a young companion from Madinah.
He served as a scribe of revelation.
He was entrusted with a task after the Prophet's passing.
He gathered the Qur'an into a written collection under Abu Bakr.
He led the standardisation under Uthman as well.
hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit, of the Ansar, was a scribe of revelation and led both the compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr and the standardisation of copies under Uthman.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of forty-five ayahs.
It is surah 50.
Its name is a single Arabic letter.
It deals extensively with resurrection and accountability.
It is reported to have been recited regularly in the Friday sermon.
hard.explain: Surah Qaf (50) opens with the single letter Qaf and deals with creation, death and resurrection. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ would recite it in the Friday sermon.
